transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I keep getting stuck on this small uneven spot around my nose and cheek. I notice it a lot in photos and under the lights at work, and even when people tell me they don’t really see it, I feel like it’s the first thing customers or my managers notice.
How much does this uneven spot on your nose and cheek bother you, and does it take up a lot of your attention throughout the day?

It bothers me a lot, even though I know it probably sounds small. I get stuck looking at that uneven spot by my nose and cheek, especially in photos or under the store lights. It takes up a lot of my attention because I keep thinking customers or my managers are noticing it first, even when people tell me they don’t really see it.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to cover it up because of the uneven spot?

Yeah, I do. On my breaks I’ll go to the bathroom and check it in the mirror, sometimes more than once. I’ll fix my hair around my face to try to hide it a little. And I catch myself comparing my face to girls who come through my line. Sometimes I spend too long doing that and end up late getting back to the register.
Is your main concern specifically about the appearance of that uneven spot on your nose and cheek, or are there other things about your appearance that also bother you in a similar way?

It’s mostly that spot, honestly. The uneven area around my nose and cheek is what I keep focusing on, especially in photos or under the store lights. Even when people say they don’t notice it, I still feel like customers or managers see that first.
Does worrying about the uneven spot on your nose and cheek cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your work, relationships, or other parts of your life?

Yeah, it does interfere, mostly at work. My manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late, and I think I’m moving slower at the register because I get stuck worrying about it. I’m trying to get promoted, so I’m scared it’s making me seem unreliable.
Do you ever feel like no matter how much you check or fix your appearance, you still can't be sure that the uneven spot doesn't stand out to others?

Yeah. I’ll check it in the bathroom mirror on my breaks, then try to fix my hair around it, but I still don’t feel sure it looks okay. Sometimes I keep comparing myself to girls in my line too, and then I end up taking too long and getting back to the register late.
Is your concern about the uneven spot mainly that it looks physically wrong or unattractive to you, or is it more about a fear that others are judging you because of it?

It’s kind of both, but it starts with me feeling like it looks wrong or uneven. Like in photos or under the store lights, I get stuck on that spot by my nose and cheek. Then I start thinking it must be the first thing customers or managers notice, even when people tell me they don’t really see it.
Do you worry about the uneven spot mostly because you feel it makes you look unattractive overall, or more because you think people are specifically judging you negatively because of it?

More because I feel like it looks wrong and stands out, I guess. Like that tiny uneven spot by my nose and cheek becomes all I can see in photos or under the store lights. Then I start worrying customers or managers are noticing it too, even when people say they don’t really see it.

Do you feel that your concern about the uneven spot is something you can't stop thinking about, even when you try, or is it more that you feel driven to check or fix it because you're worried something bad will happen if you don't?

It’s more that I can’t stop thinking about it, even when I try. I’ll tell myself it’s tiny and other people say they don’t see it, but then I see it in a photo or under the store lights and it feels like that’s the first thing customers or managers are noticing.
Has this concern about the uneven spot ever led you to avoid certain situations, like not wanting to go to work, avoiding photos, or staying away from bright lights?

Yeah… mostly at work. I don’t usually call out, but I’ll take longer on breaks because I’m trying to check it or calm myself down before going back out. My manager has noticed I’m coming back late and moving slower at the register, and I’m worried it’s making me look unreliable, especially because I’m trying to get promoted.
Has this concern about the uneven spot ever caused you to feel so distressed that it affected your ability to focus or function normally at work or in other areas of your life?

Yeah, it has. At work especially, I get distracted by it and then I’m slower. My manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late and taking longer at the register, and I’m worried it makes me look unreliable right when I’m trying to get promoted.
Do you believe the uneven spot around your nose and cheek is a significant physical defect, or do you think it might be something that most people wouldn’t really notice?

I mean… part of me knows it’s probably tiny and maybe most people wouldn’t really notice it. But when I see it in photos or under the store lights, it feels really obvious to me, like it’s the first thing customers or my managers would see.
Can you describe what goes through your mind when you notice the uneven spot? Is it more about the way it looks to you, or more about what you think others might be thinking when they see it?

It’s kind of both. I notice it in photos or under the store lights, and then I get stuck on how uneven it looks to me. But pretty quickly it turns into worrying that customers or my managers can see it too, like it’s the first thing they notice, even when other people tell me they don’t really see anything.

When you're worried about the uneven spot, is your main concern that it makes you look physically unattractive or abnormal, or is it more about the idea that people are judging or thinking negatively about you because of it?

I think it starts with how it looks to me, like it makes my face look uneven or off. But then I immediately worry that customers or my managers are seeing it too, like it’s the first thing they notice, even though people tell me they don’t see it.
About how much time do you spend thinking about the uneven spot on your nose and cheek each day, and does it interfere with your ability to do other things?

It’s not like I’m thinking about it every second, but I do get stuck on it, especially if I see myself in a photo or I’m under the lights at work. Then it’s hard to stop thinking about whether customers or my managers are noticing it. It can distract me from what I’m doing, even though people tell me they don’t really see anything.
Have you ever avoided interacting with customers or co-workers, or felt unable to fully participate in work or social situations because of your concern about the uneven spot?

Yeah… I haven’t totally stopped talking to people, but it does affect me at work. Like, I’ll take longer on breaks because I’m checking or trying to calm down, and then I move slower at the register. My manager has noticed I’m coming back late, and I’m worried it makes me look unreliable, especially because I’m trying to get promoted.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation suggests concerns about perceived physical appearance and repetitive focus on a specific body part, which points towards possible Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22). Differential includes Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (F42.2) due to preoccupation and repetitive behaviors.

The patient's preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (uneven spot on nose and cheek) is persistent and causes significant distress and impairment in work functioning, reinforcing the consideration of body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22). The presence of repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, comparing appearance to others, camouflaging) further supports this. Obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.2) remains in the differential because the behaviors could be interpreted as compulsions, but the content is more appearance-focused rather than intrusive, unwanted thoughts or urges typical of OCD. No disorders ruled out this turn.
